question: The Epley canalith repositioning manoeuvre is the first-line treatment for posterior semicircular canal BPPV and does not require any medication.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. The Epley canalith repositioning manoeuvre is the definitive treatment for posterior canal BPPV. It is a bedside procedure using sequential head position changes to move free-floating otoconia back to the utricle. No medication is needed — vestibular suppressants (e.g., prochlorperazine) are inappropriate as they do not treat the underlying mechanical problem.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The Epley manoeuvre uses a sequence of head positions to move displaced otoconia (canaliths) out of the posterior semicircular canal back into the utricle, resolving BPPV. It is highly effective (>80% success in a single session) and is the standard first-line treatment without requiring medications.
